name: Arfa Software Technology Park
assumptions: The 17-level OSM way is the tower: arcs are fitted to it, but its sharp tips are cut back to two-facet prow ends about 11 m wide with a 3 m arris, read from the Esri roof and the end-on photos; end widths are estimates, and the long axis is set to 63 m from the side-on street photo (OSM tip to tip is 74 m).
The 7-level OSM way is taken as the plan of the low glass rotunda on the north face; it is built 3 storeys (14 m) from the photos, not 7 levels.
17 floors at 4.9 m reach a body top of 83.3 m; 16 white spandrel bands are counted in the aerial photo, and floor height is an estimate.
The crown rim is cut on a slope from 106 m at the west prow (dossier) to about 98 m at the east end, estimated from the aerial and street photos.
The gothic curve of the crown panels and the height of the open screen above them (3.5 m) are fitted by eye.
Crown plant room and deck: size and position read from a leaning Esri image, height estimated.
Podium outline traced from Esri with a lean correction (it has no OSM way); height 31.5 m and six window rows from the end-on photo.
The podium south-west and south-east faces repeat the north-west window rows; they were seen only in part.
Lettering uses Blender's built-in font, not the real typefaces; the ITU emblem on the podium corner pier is left out.
Colours: dossier glass, crown and podium samples are daylight dependent; the white spandrels and pale podium are read from the aerial photo.
Boundary wall, gardens and palms are outside this model. A second tower has been approved but is not built in any photo found, so it is left out.
